main_text.p: Plato Critone: [illegible, ~60 letters] Idem Theage: [illegible, ~40 letters] ΘΕΑΓ. [illegible, ~10 letters]

Olympiodorus in nondum edita Platonis vita: [illegible, ~50 letters] Ad venaturam se exercebant, qui ad bellum redderentur aptiores. Athenaeus Libro I. [illegible, ~40 letters] [illegible, ~30 letters]
Quanta pietate colendi sint parentes secundum Deum sanxit suis Legibus Solon, poena irrogata si quis secus fecisset: haec enim eius Lex est:

Ὁ τοὺς γονέας τύπτων, ἐὰν μὴ τρέφῃ, ἐὰν μὴ παρέχῃ οἴκησιν, καὶ τὰ ἐπιτήδεια, ἄτιμος ἔστω. | Si quis parentes pulsauerit, aut non aluerit, aut tectum ad habitandum ceteraque necessaria non praebuerit, ignominiosus esto.

Appellatur haec Lex ab Atticis Iureconsultis [illegible, ~20 letters] malae tractationis parentum, non tantum natura, sed etiam adoptione, cuius meminit Lysias [illegible, ~80 letters] [illegible, ~50 letters]

Sed morte non luebat, qui in hanc Legem incurrerat, verùm ignominia notabatur: neque capite luisse dixit Lysias, mortem tamen commeritum fuisse Agoratum pronunciat, quia non tantùm in hanc malae parentum tractationis Legem commiserat, sed etiam aliorum reus erat criminum. Ignominiosus igitur erat, qui hanc Legem temerarat. Aeschynes [illegible, ~30 letters] Τιμάρχου. δίκημα (Φησί) Ῥητῶρ. [illegible, ~60 letters] Itaque expressis verbis habes apud Diogenem Laertium in Solone: [illegible, ~40 letters] Quae sit haec capitis minutio, oftendit comparatio Legum ἀπραπίας, & malae parentum tractationis, quas coniungit Demosthenes [illegible, ~30 letters] nempe [illegible, ~20 letters]. Nam cos [illegible, ~70 letters] inquit Vlpianus ad Demosthenem. Certe, ne quid de pulsatis parentibus dicam, iniquissimum est patrem egere, cum filius sit in facultatibus. Lege V.§.XIII.D. de agnoscendis & alendis liberis vel parentibus. Meminit huius Kapitis Legis Demosthenes [illegible, ~50 letters] ludens suo more dixit Aristophanes Auibus.
ἀλλ' ἔστιν ἡμῖν τοῖσιν ὅρισι νόμος [illegible, ~10 letters]
παλαιὸς ἐν τοῖς τῶν πελαργῶν χώροισιν. [illegible, ~10 letters]
ἐπεί, ὁ πατὴρ ὁ πελαργὸς ἐκπεπτωκώς [illegible, ~5 letters]

page.notes: Running head, page number and signature are clear. Much of the Greek is badly blurred and set in small type, so most Greek passages are marked illegible rather than guessed. The Latin is legible except where marked. The Greek verse notes below the text are the least certain readings. The Latin right column is set in italic and is treated as a column of the parallel block. Stains and show-through are not transcribed.
